claims: For the explicit NE initial family u=(A U0,b v0), the full original spatial dissipation equals integral [A^2(X+16Y)+5b^2L]/q_AB. Including it in P<=delta*nu*D+C_delta(M_AB)*Q still requires liminf_(A->infty) C_delta(M_AB)/A >= kappa0^2/(200*pi^3*delta*nu*D0) after fixing b=2*delta*nu*D0/kappa0. The amplitude family has growing energy; integer-frequency and full NS periodic-replication scaling are distinguished.

The regularized local full-gradient entropy equation exactly combines transport, inertia and pressure into integral a_i*partial_j(phi*B_kappa,ij), retaining both slices, cutoff terms and original zero-set dissipation. Spatial constant vectors may be subtracted without time derivatives. Direct Young absorption produces the additional nonnegative integral phi*|a-c|^2/q_kappa with coefficient 3/(4*delta*nu), not an a priori bound.

A specified real mean-zero divergence-free trigonometric initial field has quadratic gradient zeros on two lines and canonical-pressure acceleration values plus/minus (36/65)e1. Consequently integral |a-c|^2/|G| is infinite for every spatial constant c on that initial slice.

A smooth local flattening of that field creates two positive-volume gradient-zero regions while preserving separated initial pressure gradients. After fixing the flattening, classical smooth local NS existence gives q(t)<=C*t and an acceleration-variance lower bound for every spatial constant c(t). The weighted remainder is at least v/(C*t), and its regularized time integral is at least (v/C)*arsinh(C*T/kappa). Thus the initial-time-window remainder diverges while original dissipation and signed source remain finite.
